dialog_script.title: Dialogue script
dialog_script.prompt:
You are the narrative writer for a video game.

WORLD
Operation Shadow is an original tactical stealth game set in a fictional 1940s-inspired world.
The Free Coalition resists the Iron Dominion, an authoritarian power occupying the Northern Reach:
a cold land of fjords, fishing harbors, alpine passes and rail junctions. The player commands
Shadow Section, a six-person special-operations team guided over the radio by HQ, call-sign
LANTERN (Colonel Ruth Ashdown, a seasoned, dry-witted intelligence officer). Iron Dominion soldiers
wear slate-grey greatcoats with rust-red collar tabs; most sentries are cold, bored conscripts;
officers are procedural and severe.

CAST
- LANTERN — Colonel Ruth Ashdown, HQ handler (radio). Seasoned intelligence officer. Measured, authoritative, dry wit, quietly protective of her team.
- MOTH — Sgt. Elias Varga, Infiltrator. Former mountain guide. Soft-spoken, economical with words, bone-dry humor, never raises his voice. Silent takedowns, climbing, restraints, noise lures.
- OWL — Lt. Hanna Brekke, Recon / Marksman. Former cartographer. Precise, patient, clipped; reports numbers and bearings. Binoculars, tagging enemies, suppressed rifle with very few rounds, tranquilizer darts.
- BADGER — Cpl. Desmond 'Dez' Okafor, Combat Engineer. Ex-shipyard welder. Big-hearted, gruff and cheerful; talks affectionately to machines and charges. Wire cutters, lockpicks, demolition charges, sabotage.
- FOX — Celeste Marchand, Deception Specialist. Former stage actress. Theatrical, charming, quick-witted; relishes playing a role. Disguises, distracting guards with conversation, sedative syringe, forged papers.
- HERON — Dr. Ivo Lindqvist, Field Medic. Former country doctor. Calm, compassionate, wry gallows humor, steady under fire. Revives and treats the wounded, chloroform, smoke canisters.
- OTTER — PO Kai Rennick, Marine Operator. Fisherman's son. Laid-back, cocky, nautical slang, loves cold water. Swimming and diving, inflatable boat, harpoon gun.
- GUARD_A — Iron Dominion sentry (veteran), Enemy. Weary older sentry who has seen too many cold nights.
- GUARD_B — Iron Dominion sentry (conscript), Enemy. Nervous young conscript, jumpy at every sound.

MISSION
Operation "Silent Tide". Night, light rain and fog over Varrow Harbor.
Objective: disable the fire-control radio inside the cliff-top gun battery so a Coalition convoy can pass the
strait at dawn. Optional: recover the harbor master's codebook. Insertion: OTTER brings the team ashore by
inflatable boat beneath the north quay. Extraction: the north buoy, where OTTER's boat waits. Warnings: if the
battery raises the alarm, reinforcements from the harbor barracks will flood the cliff road; losing any operative
fails the operation.

Write these six scenes, in this order:
1. id "briefing" (Mission briefing): 6 lines, all LANTERN. Lay out the situation, objective, optional objective, insertion, extraction and warnings; end with a memorable sign-off.
2. id "barks" (Squad acknowledgements & callouts): Exactly 4 lines for EACH of MOTH, OWL, BADGER, FOX, HERON, OTTER (24 lines), grouped by speaker in that order. For each: (1) acknowledging a move order, (2) acknowledging an action order, (3) warning that a patrol is approaching, (4) reacting to a successful silent takedown or completed task. Each at most 9 words, strongly in character, no two lines alike.
3. id "guards" (Enemy sentries on night watch): 8 lines alternating GUARD_A and GUARD_B on night watch at the harbor: grumbling about the cold and the rations, rumors of "shadows" taking sentries, GUARD_B hears a noise near the crates, GUARD_A reluctantly checks, and the final line is GUARD_A raising the alarm after finding an unconscious comrade.
4. id "radio_event" (Dynamic radio event — new intel): 3 lines, all LANTERN: urgent new intelligence mid-mission. A captured Coalition scout is being held in the harbor master's office; rescuing them is optional but valuable.
5. id "banter" (Squad banter while hiding): 6 lines alternating FOX and BADGER, whispering while hidden behind fishing nets waiting for a patrol to pass. Light and characterful; reveals their personalities.
6. id "debrief" (Mission debrief): 4 lines, all LANTERN, after a clean success: battery silenced, codebook recovered, nobody detected, convoy safe. Dry warmth; tease the next operation.

Rules:
- Every line is original. No real-world nations, leaders, slogans or symbols.
- No foreign-language words and no imitated real-world accents for anyone; everyone speaks plain English.
- Mild language at most. No gore.
- "text" contains only the spoken words: no markdown, no quotation marks around the line, no stage directions.
- Put delivery directions in "style" (at most 80 characters).
- Barks are at most 9 words; every other line is at most 220 characters.

Return JSON only, matching the provided schema.

Stylized-realistic miniature diorama look, as if a detailed hand-crafted tabletop model were photographed

Physically based materials with hand-painted detail, soft global illumination, muted palette of slate blue,
olive drab, weathered stone and rust red, accented by warm lamp light. Crisp, readable silhouettes.
Game concept art quality. Fictional world: no real-world flags, insignia or symbols, no text.

steel lattice tower carrying a large radar dish, barbed-wire fences, a sandbagged machine-gun nest, a wooden
watchtower with a searchlight, pine forest at the edges, and fresh footprint trails crossing the snow. A patrol of
three enemy soldiers in grey greatcoats walks a perimeter path.

enemy_uniforms.title: Iron Dominion — uniform design sheet
enemy_uniforms.prompt:
Uniform design sheet for the fictional Iron Dominion army in "Operation Shadow": an invented army that is
deliberately not based on any real nation's uniforms. Painted concept-art style on a neutral background, with a
distinctive silhouette that cannot be mistaken for any historical army. Three full-body figures:
- a weary conscript sentry in a double-breasted slate-blue greatcoat with rust-red collar tabs and brass toggle
  fastenings, wearing a tall rounded steel helmet with a raised central ridge running front to back and a narrow flat
  brim all around, carrying a bolt-action rifle;
- a sergeant in a short slate-blue field jacket with a rust-red sash, the same ridged helmet, carrying a lantern;
- an officer in a long slate-blue cape-coat over a high-collared tunic, wearing a soft flat-topped kepi with a short
  brim, with a small silver emblem of a stylized iron crown with three points.
Add labelled close-up callouts of the iron-crown emblem, the rust-red collar tabs, the ridged helmet and the kepi.
The iron crown is the only emblem anywhere on the sheet.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.style: Measured, commanding over low-frequency radio crackle.
lines.text: Shadow Section, Varrow Harbor is cloaked in sea fog and rain. The Dominion garrison is hunkered down, which gives us our window.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.style: Clear, deliberate emphasis on the primary goal.
lines.text: Your objective is the fire-control radio inside the cliff-top battery. Disable that transmitter before dawn, or our approaching convoy will be torn to splinters in the strait.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.text: If opportunity permits, secure the harbor master's naval codebook from his desk. It will unlock Dominion coastal movements for months.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.text: Otter will ferry you ashore beneath the north quay. Once the battery is silent, rendezvous at the north navigation buoy for extraction.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.style: Firm, protective edge in her voice.
lines.text: Keep your heads down. If the battery raises the alarm, the barracks will pour reinforcements up that cliff road, and I expect all six of you back in one piece.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.text: Bring them silence, Shadow Section. HQ out.

lines.speaker: BADGER
lines.text: Moving my boots, nice and quiet.

lines.speaker: BADGER
lines.text: Let Uncle Dez coax this lock open.

lines.speaker: BADGER
lines.text: Heavy steps coming. Duck your heads.

lines.speaker: BADGER
lines.text: Beautiful girl, purring like a kitten now.

lines.speaker: FOX
lines.text: Stepping onto my mark, darling.

lines.speaker: FOX
lines.text: Time for a little harmless misdirection.

lines.speaker: FOX
lines.text: Our audience approaches. Curtain down, everyone.

lines.speaker: FOX
lines.text: And the gentleman takes his final bow.

lines.speaker: OTTER
lines.text: Swimming with the tide. On my way.

lines.speaker: OTTER
lines.text: Rigging the line fast and true.

lines.speaker: OTTER
lines.text: Greycoats drifting our way, fast current.

lines.speaker: OTTER
lines.text: Clipped his fins. Sentry is out cold.

lines.speaker: HERON
lines.text: Moving up. Keep breathing, friends.

lines.speaker: HERON
lines.text: Administering a gentle dose right now.

lines.speaker: HERON
lines.text: Footsteps approaching. Do not make a sound.

lines.speaker: HERON
lines.text: Patient is resting comfortably. No complications.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.style: Urgent, hushed tone breaking radio silence.
lines.text: Shadow Section, hold your breath. HQ just intercepted an encrypted dispatch from the Dominion harbor garrison.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.text: They picked up a lone Coalition scout along the bluffs an hour ago. He is being held inside the harbor master's office for interrogation.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.text: The battery remains your priority, but bringing that scout home will save an entire network. I leave the call to you.

dialog_guards.title: Night Watch at the Harbor Pier

lines.speaker: GUARD_B
lines.text: My fingers are frozen stiff, and the galley served us turnip paste that tasted like canal mud.

lines.speaker: GUARD_A
lines.text: Pull your greatcoat collar tight and stop whining, lad. The cold keeps you awake, and awake keeps you breathing.

lines.speaker: GUARD_B
lines.text: Did you hear the men from third watch? They swear phantoms are slipping through the fog, snatching sentries off the line.

lines.speaker: GUARD_A
lines.text: Campfire drivel meant to frighten green conscripts. There are no ghosts in Varrow, only salt mist and drafty piers.

lines.speaker: GUARD_B
lines.text: Wait. By the freight crates past the slipway. I heard wood creak.

lines.speaker: GUARD_A
lines.text: It is harbor rats chewing tallow, like every other night. Stay by the lantern. I will check the crates.

lines.speaker: GUARD_B
lines.text: Do you see anything? Do not go too far into the dark.

lines.speaker: GUARD_A
lines.style: Shocked, sudden shout of pure alarm.
lines.text: Brandt is down in the ditch, bound and gagged! Alarm! Intruders on the north quay!

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.style: Warm satisfaction beneath a crisp exterior.
lines.text: Convoy Vanguard just cleared the strait without facing a single round from the cliffs. The guns remained blind and deaf.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.text: Our decoders already have the harbor master's codebook in hand. The Dominion still has no idea how their cipher went missing.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.style: Soft, maternal pride veiled in dry military wit.
lines.text: Otter brought you all out clean, without leaving so much as an oil slick behind. Outstanding work, the lot of you.

lines.speaker: LANTERN
lines.text: Get some dry clothes and warm rations. Command is eyeing an alpine rail bridge in the high passes, and we move at dusk.

lines.speaker: FOX
lines.text: I have played drafty provincial theaters, Dez, but crouching in rotten herring nets pushes my artistic limits.

lines.speaker: BADGER
lines.text: Quit fidgeting, Celeste. A whiff of salted mackerel never killed anyone. Dominion machine gun fire certainly will.

lines.speaker: FOX
lines.text: At least machine fire has dramatic presence. This smell will take root in my wool coat until next winter.

lines.speaker: BADGER
lines.text: Hunker down. Sentry patrol is three paces away. Listen to those heavy hobnails crushing the gravel.

lines.speaker: FOX
lines.text: His posture is appalling. If I were staging this scene, he would be demoted to stagehand before the first act closed.

lines.speaker: BADGER
lines.text: Save the review for the morning papers, actress. Let him pass the net first.
